input.quote: 14.2.2 At-Will Termination by PB. PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
input.rationale: Section 14.2.2 is PB's only at-will exit and it fails the fallback on material terms: it does not open until SFJ has paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs, it closes entirely on receipt of the first Regulatory Approval, and the notice figure is left blank ([***]) rather than set within the 60-90 day band. In a multi-year development term that is not a usable customer convenience right. Operation 1 restores it as an express grant - "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ" - adds a pro rata refund of PB's prepayments (broadened from "fees" because this Agreement has no defined fee concept and uses Approval Payments / Buy-Out Payment), and states that SFJ has no convenience termination right during the Term. Operation 2 is a conforming fix only: because PB may now exit after Approval, the retained ARTICLE 6 carry-over is extended to Approval obtained before termination so it is not left silent. SFJ's exits (14.2.3 MAE, 14.2.5 bankruptcy, 14.2.6 Change of Control, 14.2.7 safety, 14.2.8.1 compliance breach, 14.2.9 Adverse Patent Impact, 14.2.10 JSC decision) are trigger-conditioned rather than at-will, so we do not flag them as vendor convenience rights. We target preferred because the fallback's three-months-of-fees cap has no analogue here: the retained 300% Development Cost amount is consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package under Section 11.1.1.4 and is left untouched. Residual commercial asks, flagged not redlined: the exit is unconditional but not free (300% plus continuing Approval Payments), and 14.2.10 is close to discretionary in practice.

proposal.summary: Unconditional PB termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro rata refund, express bar on SFJ convenience termination, and conforming of the retained ARTICLE 6 carry-over to a post-Approval exit.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a clear, unconditional customer exit: as drafted PB's at-will right only opens after SFJ has spent $60 million, closes at first Regulatory Approval, and leaves the notice period blank. We have made it an express termination for convenience without cause on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro rata refund of PB's prepayments, confirmed SFJ has no convenience right during the Term, and conformed the retained ARTICLE 6 carry-over so it still works if PB exits after Approval.

ops.oldText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
ops.newText: PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ, and SFJ will refund pro rata any fees or other amounts prepaid by PB for the period after the effective date of termination. SFJ has no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term.

ops.oldText: if PB elects to continue development of the Product and obtains Regulatory Approval following such termination, PB will remain obligated to pay any Approval Payments
ops.newText: if PB elects to continue development of the Product and obtains Regulatory Approval following such termination or has obtained Regulatory Approval prior to such termination, PB will remain obligated to pay any Approval Payments

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
